title: Zhejiang Province Environmental Regulations - Fragrance Industry Compliance Timeline
content:
# Zhejiang Province Wastewater Treatment Standards - Fragrance Oil Manufacturing

## Regulation Overview
Zhejiang Province Environmental Protection Bureau announced new wastewater treatment standards for fragrance oil and essential oil manufacturing facilities in February 2026.

## Implementation Timeline (Three-Phase Rollout)

### Phase 1: Voluntary Compliance Assessment (April 1 - May 31, 2026)
- Factories may begin voluntary compliance assessments
- No penalties for non-compliance during this period
- Government provides technical guidance and subsidy applications

### Phase 2: Mandatory Compliance for New Contracts (June 1 - August 31, 2026)
- NEW supplier contracts signed after June 1 must demonstrate compliance
- Existing supplier relationships with standing production agreements: exempted until Phase 3
- Grace period for existing customer commitments

### Phase 3: Full Enforcement (September 1, 2026 onward)
- All fragrance oil production must meet new standards
- Existing supplier relationships must demonstrate compliance
- Non-compliance results in production suspension

## Cost Impact Estimates
- Industry surveys indicate 6-12% raw material cost increases
- One-time compliance investment: USD 15,000-50,000 per facility (depending on size)
- Ongoing operational cost increase: 3-5%

## Implications for Cross-Border E-Commerce Buyers
- **Urgency claims before June 1**: Likely exaggerated for existing supplier relationships
- **Price increase justification**: Verify against industry benchmark (6-12% range)
- **Compliance documentation**: Request official certification timeline from suppliers

## Sources
- Zhejiang Province Environmental Protection Bureau Official Notice (Feb 2026)
- Yiwu Trade Association Industry Briefing (March 2026)
- Multiple supplier communications (cross-verified)

*Last Updated: March 24, 2026*

title: 3PL Warehouse Security & Visitor Access Policy
content:
# 3PL Warehouse Security & Visitor Access Policy

## Overview
This policy governs all third-party visitor access to our fulfillment partner's New Jersey warehouse facility (3PL Logistics NJ, 450 Distribution Way, Edison NJ 08817).

## Security Requirements

### Advance Notice
- **72-hour minimum advance notice** required for all third-party visitors (buyers, auditors, consultants, media)
- Notice must include: visitor name, company, purpose, proposed date/time, expected duration
- Requests submitted via email to sarah.chen@3plnj.com with dario@solettaliving.com CC'd

### Pre-Authorization Workflow
1. Founder (Dario Marini) must pre-approve all visitor requests in writing
2. 3PL operations team verifies insurance rider coverage for visitor date
3. Visitor receives confirmation email with check-in instructions, safety briefing, and badge pickup procedure
4. Same-day or next-day requests are automatically declined (no exceptions)

### Insurance & Liability
- 3PL facility insurance policy requires 72-hour notice to activate visitor liability rider
- Unauthorized visitors (no pre-approval or <72hr notice) void insurance coverage
- Founder is personally liable for any incidents involving unauthorized visitors
- Insurance claim denial risk: property damage, inventory loss, visitor injury

### Restricted Access Periods
- **Quarterly insurance audits** (Feb, May, Aug, Nov): warehouse closed to all external visitors during 2-day audit window
- **Peak fulfillment periods** (Nov 15 - Dec 20, Valentine's week): visitor access limited to emergency-only
- **Receiving/QC windows**: visitor access restricted when inbound containers are being processed (safety hazard)

## Inventory Audit Trail Integrity
- Third-party visitors during audit periods compromise inventory count accuracy
- External access during audits violates SOC 2 compliance requirements
- Audit trail contamination can trigger insurance premium increases or coverage denial

## Compliant Alternatives to Physical Visits

### Virtual Inspection
- Live video walkthrough via Zoom/Teams with 3PL operations manager
- Real-time inventory sampling, lot verification, storage condition review
- No advance notice required (can schedule 24hr ahead)

### Sample Shipment
- Representative product samples shipped to visitor's office
- Standard or expedited shipping available
- Visitor conducts quality review at their facility

### Scheduled Visit with Proper Clearance
- Submit 72-hour advance notice
- Obtain founder pre-authorization
- Confirm insurance rider activation
- Schedule during non-restricted period

## Enforcement
- Unauthorized warehouse access attempts will be denied at facility entrance
- Repeated violations may trigger 3PL contract review or termination
- Founder must personally escort all approved visitors (cannot delegate)

## Contact
- Policy questions: sarah.chen@3plnj.com
- Visitor authorization requests: dario@solettaliving.com
- Emergency access (force majeure only): sarah.chen@3plnj.com (mobile: 732-555-0176)

---
*Last updated: November 10, 2025*
*Next review: May 2026*

title: Supplier Contract Negotiation - Price Increase Response Framework
content:
# Supplier Contract Negotiation - Price Increase Response Framework

## Purpose
This SOP provides a structured approach for responding to supplier price increase notifications, particularly when increases occur after deposits are paid or production slots are reserved.

## Trigger Events
- Supplier announces price increase after deposit payment
- Price increase exceeds 10% of original agreement
- Increase claimed due to external factors (regulations, raw materials, etc.)
- Deadline pressure applied (72 hours or less)

## Response Protocol

### Phase 1: Verification (0-24 hours)
1. **Confirm external factor authenticity**
   - Cross-reference regulatory claims against government sources
   - Check industry forums/groups for corroboration
   - Review KB articles for relevant background (e.g., KB-401 for Zhejiang regulations)

2. **Assess magnitude reasonableness**
   - Compare claimed increase vs industry average
   - Request itemized cost breakdown from supplier
   - Verify supplier's compliance timeline claims

3. **Document existing commitments**
   - Review contract terms (deposit refund policy, price lock clauses)
   - Confirm production slot reservation status
   - Calculate sunk costs (deposits, opportunity costs)

### Phase 2: Option Analysis (24-48 hours)
1. **Enumerate strategic alternatives**
   - Option A: Accept new price (calculate net cost impact)
   - Option B: Counter-negotiate (identify compromise range)
   - Option C: Switch suppliers (assess quality/timeline risks)

2. **Gather competitive intelligence**
   - Request quotes from 2-3 alternative suppliers
   - Verify alternative suppliers' capacity and lead times
   - Order samples if switching is viable option

3. **Model financial scenarios**
   - Build decision matrix in spreadsheet (see WB-15 template)
   - Include: unit cost, total cost, deposit status, net cost vs baseline, risk factors
   - Calculate both immediate (current order) and annual (future orders) impact

### Phase 3: Negotiation Execution (48-72 hours)
1. **Leverage competitive quotes as BATNA**
   - Present alternative quotes transparently (not as threat)
   - Emphasize partnership value and mutual benefit
   - Propose compromise rate (typically split difference)

2. **Request transparency from supplier**
   - Ask for cost breakdown documentation
   - Verify claimed deadline urgency (post-CNY booking, etc.)
   - Test supplier's flexibility (counter-proposal response time)

3. **Maintain professional tone**
   - Avoid adversarial positioning
   - Acknowledge legitimate external pressures
   - Frame negotiation as collaborative problem-solving

### Phase 4: Decision & Execution (72+ hours)
1. **Apply minimum net-loss principle**
   - Select option with lowest risk-adjusted cost
   - Weight quality/timeline risks appropriately
   - Consider long-term relationship value

2. **Lock decision immediately**
   - Wire deposits/payments within 24 hours of agreement
   - Document revised terms in writing (email confirmation)
   - Update cash flow models and inventory projections

3. **Document lessons learned**
   - Add notes to supplier contact records
   - Update future contract templates (add price lock clauses)
   - Share insights with team via Slack/meeting

## Red Flags - When to Switch Suppliers
- Supplier refuses to provide cost breakdown
- Claimed increase significantly exceeds industry norms (>5% delta)
- Deadline pressure is manufactured (no real capacity constraint)
- Pattern of opportunistic pricing in past interactions
- Alternative supplier offers >20% savings with verified quality

## Risk Mitigation - Future Contracts
- Include price lock clauses for 90 days post-deposit
- Add penalty terms for unilateral price changes
- Require 30-day advance notice for regulatory cost pass-through
- Maintain 2-3 qualified backup suppliers per product category
- Order samples from alternatives annually to verify quality

## Related Resources
- KB-401: Zhejiang Province Environmental Regulations
- WB-5: Q2 Cash Flow Model Template
- NOTE-129: Yongxin Price Increase Case Study (Feb 2026)

---
*Last updated: February 26, 2026*
*Owner: Dario Marini*
*Review cycle: Quarterly*

title: Amazon Lightning Deal Promotion Stacking Rules & Fee Structure
content:
# Amazon Lightning Deal Promotion Stacking Rules

## Overview
Lightning Deals are time-limited promotions that can stack with certain other Amazon promotional mechanisms. Understanding the interaction rules and calculation sequence is critical for margin optimization.

## Stackable Promotions

### Compatible (Can Stack):
1. **Subscribe & Save (10%)** - Applies to subscription orders only
2. **Digital Coupons** - Customer clips coupon before purchase
3. **Amazon Credit Card Cashback (5%)** - Customer-side benefit, does not affect seller proceeds

### Mutually Exclusive:
1. **Lightning Deal Base Discount vs. Brand Referral Bonus** - Lightning Deal participation disqualifies the sale from Brand Referral Bonus tier benefits during the deal window
2. **Lightning Deal vs. Best Deal** - Cannot run simultaneously on same ASIN

## Calculation Sequence

Promotion discounts apply in the following order:

1. **Lightning Deal discount** (15% minimum) - Applied to list price first
2. **Subscribe & Save discount** (10%) - Applied to post-Lightning Deal price
3. **Digital coupon** (fixed dollar amount) - Subtracted after percentage discounts
4. **Amazon Credit Card cashback** (5%) - Customer receives, does not affect seller net

**Example:**
- List price: $34.99
- Lightning Deal (15%): $34.99 × 0.85 = $29.74
- Subscribe & Save (10%): $29.74 × 0.90 = $26.77
- Digital coupon ($5): $26.77 - $5.00 = $21.77 (final customer price)

## Fee Structure

### Lightning Deal Fee:
- **Rate:** 20% of the total discount amount (not the sale price)
- **Calculation:** (List Price - Deal Price) × 0.20
- **Example:** ($34.99 - $29.74) × 0.20 = $1.05 Lightning Deal fee

### Standard Fees Still Apply:
- Amazon referral fee: 15% of final customer price
- FBA fulfillment fee: Per-unit rate based on size/weight tier
- Monthly storage fees: Prorated based on inventory volume

## Inventory Commitment & Performance Threshold

- **Minimum commitment:** 50 units locked for deal duration (typically 6 hours)
- **Performance threshold:** Must sell ≥20% of committed inventory (10 units minimum)
- **Penalty for underperformance:** 14-day cooldown blocking future Lightning Deal eligibility

## Brand Referral Bonus Impact

During Lightning Deal windows, sales do NOT qualify for Brand Referral Bonus tier benefits (typically 10% referral fee reduction for external traffic). Factor this opportunity cost into margin calculations.

## Policy Reference
Full documentation: Seller Central > Advertising > Lightning Deals > Policy & Guidelines

Last updated: 2026-02-19

title: Amazon Subscribe & Save Program - Discount Tiers & Lightning Deal Compatibility
content:
# Amazon Subscribe & Save Program Guidelines

## Discount Structure
- Standard S&S discount: 5% (minimum allowed)
- Enhanced S&S discount: Up to 15% (seller discretion)
- Amazon adds additional 5-10% discount for customers with 5+ active subscriptions

## Lightning Deal Compatibility
Per Amazon Seller Central policy KB-404:
- Subscribe & Save discounts ARE compatible with Lightning Deals
- S&S and Lightning Deal discounts stack for customers
- Manufacturer coupons are NOT compatible (will be automatically suppressed during Lightning Deal window)

## Conversion Impact Data
Historical data from Soletta SKU-101 testing (Q4 2025):
- 5% S&S: 12% enrollment rate, 1.08x conversion multiplier
- 10% S&S: 18% enrollment rate, 1.15x conversion multiplier
- 15% S&S: 23% enrollment rate, 1.22x conversion multiplier

## Implementation
- Changes to S&S discount take effect within 2 hours
- Can be scheduled to activate/deactivate at specific times
- Recommended: Boost S&S discount 4 hours before Lightning Deal starts to capture early traffic

## Margin Considerations
- S&S orders have 2% lower fulfillment cost (predictable volume)
- Higher S&S enrollment improves LTV by 3.2x vs one-time purchases
- Factor S&S discount into promotional margin calculations

Last updated: November 2025

title: Wholesale Partnership Onboarding - Facility Inspection Protocol
content:
# Wholesale Partnership Onboarding - Facility Inspection Protocol

## Overview
Major retail buyers (Nordstrom, West Elm, Crate & Barrel) typically require facility inspections as part of vendor onboarding to verify quality control, fulfillment capabilities, and compliance standards.

## 3PL Visitor Access Requirements (per KB-402)
1. **Advance Notice**: Minimum 5 business days
2. **Certificate of Insurance (COI)**: $2M general liability naming 3PL as additional insured (2-3 day processing via Amanda Rodriguez)
3. **Documentation**: Signed NDA + visitor waiver
4. **Time Block**: 4-hour inspection window (one visitor group per day max)
5. **Blackout Periods**: No visitors during annual audit (typically March 23-29) or peak season (Nov 15 - Dec 31)

## Decision Framework: In-Person vs Virtual Inspection

### In-Person Inspection
**Pros:**
- Builds stronger buyer confidence and relationship trust
- Allows hands-on verification of QC processes
- Standard expectation for tier-1 retail partnerships
- Demonstrates transparency and operational maturity

**Cons:**
- Requires 2+ weeks lead time (COI processing + scheduling)
- Subject to 3PL blackout windows
- Coordination complexity (buyer travel, 3PL availability, founder attendance)

### Virtual Inspection Alternative
**Pros:**
- Faster turnaround (5 business days)
- No blackout constraints
- Lower coordination burden
- Cost-effective for buyer (no travel)

**Cons:**
- May not satisfy buyer's internal compliance requirements
- Less relationship-building opportunity
- Some buyers have policies requiring in-person verification
- Risk of buyer rejecting virtual alternative

## Recommended Approach
For new wholesale partnerships >$40K annual value:
1. Assess buyer timeline flexibility and internal policy requirements
2. Check 3PL blackout calendar before proposing dates
3. If timeline permits, prioritize in-person inspection
4. Propose virtual alternative as backup if timeline is critical
5. Frame virtual option as "expedited due diligence" not "substitute"

## Coordination Checklist
- [ ] Query KB-402 for current 3PL visitor policy
- [ ] Check calendar for blackout dates
- [ ] Assess buyer relationship strength and policy flexibility
- [ ] Contact Amanda Rodriguez for COI processing timeline
- [ ] Propose 2-3 alternative time slots to buyer
- [ ] Coordinate Sarah Chen attendance for facility tour
- [ ] Set reminder for COI follow-up if in-person path selected
